messages:
maya: FYI incoming support ticket from @acme — Console hourly metrics are delayed by ~3 hours, some tenants showing zero usage since ~10:00 UTC.

nina: Customer is on a quick call, they're seeing blank charts and missing hourly rows in the Analytics UI.

maya: Ticket #SUP-4821. Initial check: alerts show `ingest-consumer` consumer-group lagging heavily on topic `tenant-usage-hourly`.

support-bot: Alert: consumer-group ingest-consumer lag > 50k msgs (topic tenant-usage-hourly) at 2025-11-05T12:20Z

sam: I'll grab consumer logs and check k8s. Can someone check pod restarts/ooms?

eric: Running `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=ingest-consumer` -> 3/4 Ready, one CrashLoopBackOff.

eric: Logs from crashing pod:
```
kubectl -n prod logs ingest-consumer-7f9c -c consumer
ERROR: OOMKilled while processing tenant 1234
...\nThrottleException: broker temporarily throttling produce requests
```

maya: I also see a short spike in Kafka produce latency around 10:12-10:18Z. Could be broker-side throttling or controller rebalance.

sam: Can someone run `kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --group ingest-consumer --describe` and paste output?

nina: Remote check shows leader reassignments and retries around 10:15Z.

sam: `--describe` shows lag per partition ~60k for several partitions; lag origin ~10:15 UTC.

sam: Root cause hypothesis: the canary rollout caused GC/oom on one consumer pod, it crashed, the HPA didn't scale fast enough, backlog accumulated, and downstream rollup jobs fell behind -> Console hourly rollups missing.

eric: Short-term mitigation: increase replicas to 6 and restart the CrashLoop pod after grabbing heap dump. Also pin consumer JVM GC flags to reduce pause.

maya: Notifying customer that we're investigating. ETA to get backlog draining ~1.5–3h depending on throughput.

infra-bot: Deploy event: canary deployment started for ingest-consumer at 2025-11-05T12:35Z (sha: abc123).

sam: That canary overlapped with the spike. Can we revert the canary?

eric: Reverting now; will check if GC spikes stop.

infra-bot: Revert completed for ingest-consumer (rollback to sha: def456) at 12:37Z.

sam: Post-revert pods look stable, but backlog persists. Estimated drain time at current throughput ~2.5h.

maya: We need a plan to surface the missing rows in Console — any backfill options?

eric: We can run the hourly backfill DAG for the affected window: 
```
airflow trigger_dag analytics_hourly_backfill --conf '{"start":"2025-11-05T10:00:00Z","end":"2025-11-05T13:00:00Z","tenants":["acme"]}'
```
That will reprocess raw topic messages into rollups.

sam: I'll queue a prioritized backfill for the top 10 impacted tenants and watch throughput.

nina: Customer asked about billing — billing reads from rollups, so charges may be missing until backfill finishes. Recommend a provisional billing note from Finance/CS.

maya: Pinging finance & CS to flag provisional invoice.

sam: Observed current backfill progress: 15% complete, ETA ~2h. Increasing consumer instances improved throughput ~1.8x.

eric: Follow-ups: 1) Run backfill for affected windows (in progress). 2) Increase replicas + resources (done). 3) Capture heap dump + tune GC. 4) Add HPA/Autoscaler tuning and livenessProbe to prevent extended slow death loops. 5) Postmortem to verify canary interaction with broker throttling — owning infra item.

maya: I'll update SUP-4821 and send an interim note to customer in 10m with link to the backfill job and ETA.

nina: Customer acknowledged on call, wants notification when Console shows hourly rows again. :thumbsup: 

sam: Backfill progress update 30m later: 48% processed, lag falling but still a few partitions with high lag. Monitoring throughput now.

maya: Keeping thread open for PM and postmortem assignment. Will close once dashboards reflect the missing rows and ticket updated.

eric: Postmortem owners: infra (eric), eng (sam), support (maya). Will schedule RFC for consumer rollout guardrails.

maya: Thanks everyone.
